band_composition_vs_existing_panel.caveat: These are the OLD panel's per-band means applied to new weights. The reserve is drawn from the training population, so its per-band means should be better than an externally mined cohort's; the reweighting DIRECTION is the claim here, not the absolute value.
band_composition_vs_existing_panel.correction_to_the_earlier_estimate: An earlier note said support-matching would move identity NLL from 2.62 to about 1.94. That conflated the MATCHED view with the SUPPORTED-scaffold view; 1.94 is band 25+ alone. Applying training weights to the same per-band means gives 2.74, i.e. matching moves the number +0.12, slightly WORSE than the old raw mean rather than 0.69 nats better. The re-freeze buys an interpretable number, not a flattering one.
band_composition_vs_existing_panel.finding: The existing panel is BIMODAL against the training population: it over-represents band 0 (42.6% vs 19.3%) and band 25+ (22.0% vs 10.4%) while under-representing band 1-4 (13.7% vs 43.4%), which is the hardest band at 2.93. That is the accidental support composition, quantified.

not_a_causal_claim: Support is not asserted to cause the gap. Bands 0 and 1-4 are indistinguishable and the benefit concentrates at 25+, consistent with a latent typical-chemistry axis. The split only has to stop representing that axis by accident.

views.external_cohort: the existing 16-shard validation panel, retained as a cross-cohort test and NOT a selection input
views.matched: all bands, reweighted by matched_selection_weights; the checkpoint-selection number
views.new_scaffold: band 0 only; extrapolation to unseen chemistry
views.supported_scaffold: band 25+ only; new molecules in familiar series
